gold_assessment.reasoning: Generated cc-001 documents shortness of breath as the chief complaint. The C-section timing and rest status are not included but the core complaint (SOB) is captured.

Gold specifies SOB at rest with acute onset while watching TV; no generated HPI fact explicitly states that the SOB is at rest (rather than with exertion or otherwise) or that it is SOB at rest as such, only that it began while watching TV about 1 hour ago.
Gold: unproductive cough one day prior to presentation. Generated hpi-002: cough started yesterday. This matches the timing; productivity is not addressed but not contradicted.
Gold: dyspnea is non-positional. No generated fact states that dyspnea is non-positional or equivalent.

Gold: C-section 2–3 weeks ago, no complications, baby well. Generated hpi-006 and hpi-007: postpartum 4 weeks after C-section and baby present and well. Timing differs but core facts of prior C-section and baby well are captured; complications not discussed. Treated as covered on main elements.

Gold: patient not taking blood thinners. Generated facts do not assert that the patient is taking blood thinners; no explicit generated medication contradicts this. However, this same statement appears under Medications as med-001 in Gold and is only indirectly reflected. Since absence of blood thinners is not contradicted, and no generated fact states use of anticoagulants, the content is effectively preserved. (Also see med-001).
Gold: patient denies fever. Generated ros-004: ROS negative for fever. Direct match.
Gold: patient denies chills. No generated ROS fact addresses chills.
Gold: denies chest pain. Generated ros-003: ROS negative for chest pain; also hpi-005: no chest pain reported. Content is captured.

Gold: denies pain on inspiration. Generated hpi-003: chest feels sore on deep inspiration. This is the opposite (presence of soreness/pain vs denial), so the gold fact is not reproduced but is explicitly contradicted. Because the instruction is whether the gold fact is captured, it is not captured; therefore this should be marked OMITTED, but with explicit contradiction in generated facts. Reclassifying: OMITTED.
Gold: no significant past medical history. Generated pmh-002: no other medical problems documented. This reflects absence of other PMH.

Gold: patient not on anticoagulant therapy (blood thinners). No generated medication fact lists any anticoagulant use, and none contradict this. The specific statement is not re-documented but is not altered; treated as covered in substance.
Gold: allergic to ibuprofen. Generated allergy-001: allergic to ibuprofen, reaction not documented. This fully captures the fact and adds that reaction is not documented.

Gold: HR via telephone ~120 bpm, tachy, regular. Generated physical-001 and physical-002 describe patient counts and ‘slightly fast’ heart but give no HR value or characterization as tachycardic regular at ~120. Thus the gold physical detail is not captured.
Gold: mother has history of blood clots in legs. No generated fact mentions this family history.
Gold: PE considered in differential. Generated asm-002: PE included in differential. Directly captured.

Gold: plan is further examination and investigations in an acute setting. Generated plan-001 and plan-004 advise urgent hospital evaluation and consideration of cardiopulmonary causes but do not explicitly state a plan of further examination and investigation in an acute setting as a formal plan item. The spirit is similar, but wording in gold refers to internal clinical plan, while generated focuses on advice to patient; still, reasonably this is conceptually covered. Reclassifying: COVERED – the essential plan for acute setting further evaluation is present in plan-001/plan-004.

gen_assessment.reasoning: Gold only says acute onset while watching TV; it does not specify ‘about 1 hour ago’ or that the patient was sitting. Time and posture are added details not in gold, but not contradictory.
Generated: chest feels sore on deep inspiration. Gold ROS explicitly states ‘no pain on inspiration.’ These directly conflict.
Heart racing sensation is not described in gold facts. No conflict, but it is new information.

Generated: postpartum 4 weeks after C-section. Gold: C-section 2–3 weeks ago (HPI) and 4 weeks ago (CC); the specific gold HPI fact says 2–3 weeks. Dating here conflicts with that gold HPI detail, though it aligns with the chief complaint note. Since we must compare to all gold, the 4-week timing contradicts hpi-004.

Generated PMH frames C-section 4 weeks ago as past history. Gold HPI notes C-section 2–3 weeks ago; timing differs and location of documentation differs. The existence of a C-section is supported (hpi-004), but the 4-week interval is inconsistent with that HPI detail and consistent with chief complaint. Because gold has conflicting C-section timings (4 weeks in CC vs 2–3 weeks in HPI), this is best treated as ADDITION with internal dating ambiguity rather than strict contradiction to the overall record.
Gold only states no blood thinners, and does not mention codeine. Codeine use for postpartum pain is new information, not in gold, but not contradictory.
Timing of last codeine dose (not taken for about a week) is not present in gold facts; new but not conflicting.

Statement that no one else is with the patient at home is not in gold; new but not conflicting.

Gold describes SOB in the chief complaint and HPI but does not explicitly list ROS positive for SOB. This is a formal ROS restatement of something otherwise present; treated as added documentation detail rather than directly supported ROS entry.
Gold HPI notes a cough one day prior, but does not explicitly state ‘ROS positive for cough.’ This is consistent but is an added ROS categorization.
Gold only has HR via telephone ~120 bpm, tachy, regular. Patient counting 30 heartbeats in an interval is not mentioned; additional exam detail, not conflicting.
Clinician statement that heart was ‘slightly fast’ is not in gold, but is compatible with tachycardia; new descriptive detail.

Gold assessment includes PE and shortness of breath in the postpartum period (by context) but does not explicitly phrase the assessment as ‘acute SOB in postpartum period four weeks after C-section.’ This is a synthesized summary including the 4-week timing; the SOB and postpartum status are supported, but the precise phrasing is additional composition and timing is discordant with HPI’s 2–3 weeks. Treated as ADDITION.
